headline: Six new studies, and the Fathers checked line by line
body: The theology library grew by six long-form studies this week, and a new shelf opened beside the others: the worship of the Church. The Divine Liturgy of St John Chrysostom is now walked in the order it is actually served, from the cutting of the Lamb at the table of preparation through to communion, and the vestments have their own study, each garment with its name, its root in Exodus, and the prayer the priest says while putting it on.

Alongside them, four studies from the dogma side: why the Church does not receive the Council of Florence, what St Theodore the Studite was really asking of Rome when he wrote to it from exile, whether St Justin Martyr can fairly be called a subordinationist, and how the Cross both heals and pays without turning God into a creditor.

The part we are most glad about is the part you cannot see. Every quotation in those six was checked word by word against the public-domain edition it cites, and two were removed because they could not be confirmed. One of them was a well-known text that turned out to be a modern wording wearing a very old citation. We would rather print less and have it be true.
